ajay: Heads-up — seeing a burst of GPU ECC corrections and a few Xid resets on a handful of us-west-2 inference nodes. Current oncall spends ~30–45m per flaky card. Can we agree a concise log collection + parsing recipe so triage is <10m? :eyes:

simone: Which nodes and can you paste a couple of raw lines from dmesg/journalctl + nvidia-smi output?

ajay: nodes: gw-infer-uw2-07, gw-infer-uw2-12, gw-infer-uw2-13. Example dmesg/journalctl snippets: 

```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:01:00): 31, GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 12346.002345] NVRM: RmInitAdapter failed! (0x24:0xff)
Mar  3 12:05:23 gw-infer-uw2-07 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:01:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
```

And nvidia-smi excerpts: 
```
$ nvidia-smi -q -d ECC
GPU 0000:01:00.0
    ECC Errors
        Volatile:  corrected: 153, uncorrected: 0
        Aggregate:  corrected: 153, uncorrected: 0
GPU 0000:02:00.0
    ECC Errors
        Volatile:  corrected: 12, uncorrected: 1
```

We also saw frequent "GPU has fallen off the bus" and intermittent nv-host engine resets in journalctl.

:tess: Ok — here's a short checklist + commands I use to collect everything fast (run on node or via sudo remote exec):

1) capture kernel ring + time-shifted dmesg
```
dmesg -T --level=err,warn | egrep -i "nvrm|xid|gpu|reset" > /tmp/gpu-dmesg-$(hostname)-$(date -u +%s).log
journalctl -k --since "-1 hour" | egrep -i "nvrm|xid|gpu|nvhost|nvidia" >> /tmp/gpu-dmesg-$(hostname)-$(date -u +%s).log
```
2) nvidia tooling
```
nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,ECC,POWER,PCI,RETIREMENT > /tmp/nvidia-smi-$(hostname)-$(date -u +%s).log
nvidia-smi pmon -c 1 >> /tmp/nvidia-pmon-$(hostname).log  # quick process snapshot
```
3) collect syslogs + hw details
```
cp /var/log/messages /tmp/ || true
lspci -vvv | egrep -A3 "VGA|3D" > /tmp/lspci-$(hostname).log
sudo dmidecode -t slot > /tmp/dmidecode-$(hostname).log
```
4) bundle and upload
```
tar czf /tmp/gpu-triage-$(hostname)-$(date -u +%s).tgz /tmp/gpu-* && aws s3 cp /tmp/gpu-triage-$(hostname)-*.tgz s3://redwood-gpu-triage/${TEAM:-eng-infra}/
```

lisa-oncall: To speed parsing I use a tiny parser that extracts Xid codes, timestamps, and GPU PCI id then buckets them. Here's a compact awk pipeline that has saved me time: 
```
# get lines with Xid and show time + pci + xid
journalctl -k --since "-2 hours" | grep -i "Xid (PCI" | awk -F"\"\"" '{print $1}' | sed -E 's/.*PCI:([0-9a-f:]+).*Xid.*: ([0-9]+)/\1 \2/' | sort | uniq -c
```
That output quickly shows how many Xid 31 vs 79 we saw per PCI device.

simone: If we want structured parsing we can push kernel messages to a central Fluentd/Vector pipeline that tags Xid/ECC lines, convert to JSON and expose counts via Prometheus using the textfile collector. Quick python snippet to parse dmesg file into CSV: 
```
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import re,sys
pat = re.compile(r"\[(?P<ts>[^\]]+)\].*PCI:?(?P<pci>[0-9a-f:]+).*Xid.*:?\s*(?P<xid>\d+)", re.I)
for l in sys.stdin:
    m = pat.search(l)
    if m:
        print(f"{m.group('ts')},{m.group('pci')},{m.group('xid')}")
```
Pipe dmesg/journal into it and you get CSV you can feed to scripts.

ajay: Nice. For runbook purposes we should capture a minimal set in every pager wakeup: dmesg -T + last 2h journalctl -k, nvidia-smi -q, lspci, and node exporter /metrics snapshot. We should also snapshot kube state for pods using GPUs so we can route work off the node quickly.

tess: Agree. Automation ideas:
- run a short collection job automatically when ECC corrected count delta > threshold or Xid appears (e.g., via alertmanager webhook)
- push parsed Xid counts to a prometheus metric like redwood_gpu_xid_total{pci=\"0000:01:00\"} 
- have alert playbook auto-taint the node and post a link to collected archive

infra-bot: Started gpu-triage job on gw-infer-uw2-12, collection id ct-202403xx-09 (uploaded to s3).

lisa-oncall: Triage checklist (2–10 min fast flow):
1) confirm Xid/ECC spikes in collected logs
2) check PCIe resets and "has fallen off the bus" patterns
3) check GPU thermal/power & ECC time series (prom)
4) if persistent -> kubectl cordon + drain node -> schedule replacement or RMA card
5) if transient -> monitor, increase ECC thresholds and mark node noisy (label)

simone: Drain command we use: 
```
kubectl cordon <node>
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m
```
Then we annotate the node with gpu:flaky and create an infra ticket for hardware swap.

ajay: Perfect — can someone take these snippets and make a short runbook doc + one-click collection job (lambda/agent)? I can test on gw-infer-uw2-13 tomorrow AM.

tess: I'll draft the runbook and automate an alertmanager webhook to trigger the collection + attach S3 link in the alert.

ajay: Thanks all — if we standardize this we should get triage down to <10m and faster replacement decisions. :thumbsup:
